# Workflows

Work is committed straight to `dev` after the local checks, one pull request carries `dev` into `stage` (merge commit), and `stage` goes to `main` with a merge commit ([CONTRIBUTING.md#branches](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#branches)). [`scripts/ci/dev-paused`](../../scripts/ci/dev-paused) is `false`: the one switch, read by the branch name check and `release.yml` through `scripts/ci/dev-paused.sh`. Set it to `true` to pause `dev` again: `stage` then takes feature branches too, and `release.yml` stops merging `main` into `dev`.

| Workflow | Trigger | What it guards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`ci.yml`](ci.yml) | push to `main`, `stage` or `dev` (not the commits `release.yml` pushes, which start no workflow), PRs into any of them, a merge queue, manual | One job per concern: `lint` (Biome, hygiene, documentation links, changelog section, shellcheck), `typecheck`, `test` (with coverage thresholds) and `build` plus a check that the built server holds one board cache (`scripts/ci/single-board-cache.ts`) and SSR smoke (`scripts/ci/smoke.sh`) on the Node version in `.nvmrc` and on Node 24, `browser tests (chromium-desktop)`, `browser tests (chromium-mobile)`, `browser tests (desktop-safari)`, `browser tests (iphone)` and `browser tests (ipad)` (Playwright and axe against that build, sharded so each finishes well inside its 25-minute step timeout: Chromium runs `desktop` in one shard with the larger layout screens (`Galaxy Z Fold 7`, `Galaxy Tab S9`, `Pixel 7 landscape`) and `mobile` and `tablet` in another with the phone ones (`Galaxy S9+`, `Pixel 10`, `Galaxy Z Fold 7 Cover`), because the three Chromium projects (`desktop`, `mobile` and `tablet`) together took 8.3 to 9 minutes before the tilt performance runs were added, and over 10 on a slower run, which the old 10-minute step timeout could not hold; the layout screens run only the `@layout` tests. WebKit has one device per shard with its layout screens (`iphone` also runs `iPhone SE (3rd gen)`, `iPhone 17 Pro Max` and `iPhone 17 Pro landscape`, `ipad` also runs `iPad Mini`), and Chromium downloads its browser while the WebKit shards run in Playwright's image, pinned by digest, which has WebKit and its system libraries, because fetching them from apt was too slow and timed out; a `Check the browser` step fails with a clear message if the image and the `@playwright/test` version in the lockfile differ), `browser tests (history build)` (builds with `VITE_STATUS_HISTORY=1` and runs the `@history`-tagged tests on Chromium), `browser tests (node server)` (runs the `@node-server` tests on Chromium, desktop and phone, against `src/node/serve.ts`, the production server the Docker image runs: cache headers, compression, the security headers), `docker image` (builds the Dockerfile for amd64 and runs it read-only with `scripts/ci/image-smoke.sh`: healthy, smoke-tested, clean exit on `SIGTERM`; nothing is pushed), `commit messages`, `branch name` (the naming convention, and that `main` takes pull requests only from `stage` and bump.sh's `release/vX.Y.Z`, and `stage` only from `dev` (and `chore/sync-main`); while `dev` is paused, `stage` takes feature branches too: `scripts/ci/dev-paused` is the switch), and `workflow lint` (actionlint and zizmor). `CI OK` passes only when all of them did and is the one check to require. Job summaries show coverage and client bundle sizes |
| [`scorecard.yml`](scorecard.yml) | push to `main`, branch protection changes, weekly, manual | OpenSSF Scorecard: grades pinning, token permissions, branch protection, review and the rest of the supply chain, uploads findings to code scanning and publishes the score behind the README badge |
| [`codeql.yml`](codeql.yml) | push to `main`, `stage` or `dev`, PRs into any of them, weekly, manual | Static security and quality analysis of the TypeScript sources and of the workflows themselves (CodeQL's `actions` language) |
| [`dependency-review.yml`](dependency-review.yml) | PRs into `main`, `stage` or `dev` | Blocks high or critical vulnerabilities in dependency changes. Warns, and does not fail, when Dependency graph is off |
| [`ci-triage.yml`](ci-triage.yml) | completion of CI, CodeQL or Dependency review on a PR | One self-updating comment per PR naming the failed job, the failed step and its likely cause, plus a `ci-failed` label. Reads the API only and never runs PR code. Active once on `main` |
| [`source-health.yml`](source-health.yml) | hourly, manual | Calls the real vendor endpoints (three attempts a run, 20 s and then 90 s apart after a timeout or network error) and keeps one `source-health` issue open per broken collector or vendor release feed (reported apart, as "GitLab releases"), closing it on recovery. A source gets its issue only after it fails in two consecutive runs at least 30 minutes apart, so a vendor blip opens nothing and a real outage is reported one run (hours) later; the first failing run is noted in a closed `source-health-state` issue (label created on first use, issue also found by a marker in its body). With the `PRODUCTION_URL` repository variable set, also checks the production board's `/readyz` and keeps one `deploy-health` issue open while it is not 200 |
| [`screenshot.yml`](screenshot.yml) | manual, PRs that change it | Builds and runs the board where the vendors are reachable, captures it with live data, and uploads `board-screenshot` for the README's `docs/board.png` |
| [`release.yml`](release.yml) | every push to `main`; Run workflow; a `vX.Y.Z` tag | Releases what reaches `main`, promoted from `dev` through `stage`; merges into `dev` or `stage` never release. The Conventional Commits since the last tag pick the version (breaking → major, `feat` → minor, `fix`/`perf`/`revert` → patch, anything else, `release` commits included → no release). Checks the release is on `main`, has a `CHANGELOG.md` section and passes typecheck, tests and build, then commits the version bump to `main`, tags it, drafts the GitHub Release, then signs its source archive and publishes it: a separate `sign release` job attaches `status-page-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz` and its keyless Sigstore bundle (`.sigstore.json`), checked with cosign before upload ([CONTRIBUTING.md#verifying-a-release](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#verifying-a-release)). Two more jobs publish the Docker image for the tag: `build and push image` (the Dockerfile at the tag for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, smoke-tested before the push, to `ghcr.io/<owner>/status-page:X.Y.Z`, and `:latest` for the newest version, with provenance and an SBOM; `packages: write`, no `id-token`) and `sign image` (cosign over the pushed digest, verified; `packages: write` and `id-token: write`, no project code). A tag from before the Dockerfile existed is skipped with a notice ([CONTRIBUTING.md#publishing-the-docker-image](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#publishing-the-docker-image)) Run workflow also takes a manual bump, or a `version` and `commit` to backfill an older release. A push that fails fails the run with its cause (a ruleset rejection, `GH013`, says to release with `bump.sh` and a pull request into `main`, or for `stage` and `dev` to sync through `chore/sync-main`; [CONTRIBUTING.md#releases](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#releases)); only a branch that really moved meanwhile is handled quietly. Merges `main` back into `stage` and then `dev` (skips `dev` only while it is paused), and when that merge moves `stage`, starts `deploy.yml` on it too (the merge push itself starts no workflow; `dev` deploys nothing) |
| [`deploy.yml`](deploy.yml) | push to `main` or `stage` (not `dev`), PRs into `main`, `stage` or `dev`, `release.yml` after it syncs `stage`, manual on `main` or `stage` only | Builds the Worker for Cloudflare: each Worker isolate collects on request and caches in memory. Every build checks that the built Worker holds one board cache (`scripts/ci/single-board-cache.ts`) and runs the Worker in workerd (smoke test with `--require-asset-cache`); a PR also runs a credential-free `wrangler deploy --dry-run`. A push to `main` deploys the Worker in the `production` environment; a push to `stage` creates or updates a Worker Preview of it named `stage` (`wrangler preview`) in the `staging` environment, served at `https://stage.status.szolotov.com`. Either is then smoke-tested (`scripts/ci/smoke.sh --require-ready --ready-wait 60 --require-asset-cache`; a production deploy also passes `--expect-version`, so it waits until the version wrangler reported answers in `X-Worker-Version`; either way a board still stale or all-Unknown after collection fails too) and a failed production deploy is rolled back to the previous version, waiting until the failed version stops answering. A failed preview is not rolled back, since it never receives production traffic. The API token is an environment secret, seen only by the deploy, preview and rollback steps, in a job that installs with `--ignore-scripts`, verifies that install's registry signatures and runs no build or project JavaScript |
| [`pr-title.yml`](pr-title.yml) | PRs into `main`, `stage` or `dev`, including title edits | The PR title is a Conventional Commit (`release: vX.Y.Z` for a `bump.sh` release pull request). Guards the titles of the `dev` → `stage` and `stage` → `main` pull requests (and Dependabot's into `dev`); `release.yml` reads the commit subjects that the merge commits carry from `dev` to `main`, not these titles |
| [`base-images.yml`](base-images.yml) | PRs that change `compose.yaml`, its script or the dependencies; weekly; manual | Runs `compose.yaml` against the real `ci-node22`, `ci-node24` and `ci-security` images, so a base-image change that breaks this repository shows up here first |

Jobs that need Node use the shared [`../actions/setup`](../actions/setup/action.yml) action: Node from `.nvmrc` (or a given version), pnpm pinned to `packageManager` (installed by Corepack, which checks the sha512 in it, through `scripts/ci/pnpm-pin.sh`), `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the registry signature check (`scripts/ci/audit-signatures.sh`). `deploy.yml` and `release.yml` install explicitly instead, so the workflows that publish can be read on their own, and neither restores a shared package cache.

Every check in `ci.yml` has a local equivalent:

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm run check   # lint, typecheck, tests, hygiene and links
pnpm run test:coverage     # unit tests against the coverage thresholds
pnpm run build && pnpm run test:e2e   # browser tests; `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` once
./scripts/ci/pnpm-pin.sh check   # packageManager is pnpm@X.Y.Z+sha512.<128 hex>
./scripts/ci/audit-signatures.sh   # registry signatures of every locked package, after `pnpm install`
./scripts/ci/hygiene.sh  # line endings, trailing whitespace, final newline, no `any`, no raw hex
actionlint && uvx zizmor .github   # the workflow lint job: syntax, then a security audit
./scripts/ci/links.sh    # relative links in the Markdown docs
node --experimental-strip-types scripts/ci/single-board-cache.ts dist/server   # after `pnpm run build`: one board cache in the server build
./scripts/ci/smoke.sh http://127.0.0.1:4173   # after `pnpm run preview`: the smoke test CI and the deploy run
./scripts/ci/verify-deploy.sh   # by hand after a deploy (no workflow runs it): headers, robots and TLS of the live hosts
./scripts/ci/commits.sh origin/dev..HEAD   # origin/stage..HEAD for a promotion
./scripts/ci/commits.sh --subject "feat: add a feed" --base dev --head feature/add-a-feed   # a PR title and its branches, as pr-title.yml checks it (a release: title passes only from release/vX.Y.Z into main)
./scripts/ci/branch.sh "$(git branch --show-current)" stage   # the branch name and its base, as CI checks them (dev, once it is back)
./scripts/release/next.sh level "v$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")..origin/stage"   # the bump merging stage into main would release
./scripts/ci/release-notes.sh           # the CHANGELOG.md section release.yml would publish
pnpm exec vitest run scripts/release/push.test.ts   # release.yml's pushes against a bare remote with a pre-receive hook that rejects like a ruleset (GH013): moved, rejected, and dev paused
node --experimental-strip-types scripts/ci/source-health.ts   # live vendor check, exits 1 on any failure
```
